title: Access Log Data Exploration
aim: To load, inspect, and explore unstructured web honeypot access log data (cj.log), determine its schema, verify encoding, and audit record count integrity.
input: Raw honeypot text file (cj.log), 215.40 MB (225,867,389 bytes), 2,062,365 physical lines.
process: Streamed file line-by-line via memory-safe generator, handled concatenated '][' lines, deserialized JSON arrays, validated 8 positional attributes, and reconciled physical vs extracted line counts.
methods_tools: Python Streaming Generator, Regex Delimiter Splitting (']['), json.loads Deserialization, Accounting Reconciliation Auditing, Matplotlib Visualization.
result: 2,062,361 extracted records from 2,062,365 physical lines (934 blank, 911 multi-record lines expanded to 1,841). 31 malformed records (99.9985% parsing success). 16,680 unique client IPs across 407 calendar days.

title: Convert Unstructured Logs into Structured Dataset
aim: To transform unstructured honeypot access logs into a canonical 13-column tabular dataset, enforcing strict data typing and missing value identification.
process: Extracted 8 source attributes, synthesized 5 standard web fields (request_type, status_code, resource_requested, bytes_sent, referrer), and enforced a consistent 13-column relational schema.
methods_tools: Pandas DataFrame Vectorization, Positional Schema Mapping, Missing Value Quantification, Data Quality Auditing.
result: 2,062,361 structured rows in 13 canonical columns. Identified 18,433,649 explicit missing values in optional/synthesized HTTP attributes with 100% parsing fidelity.

title: Data Cleaning & Preprocessing
aim: To clean the structured access logs by removing exact duplicate records, imputing missing values, parsing timestamps, and normalizing URL paths.
process: Deduplicated records based on exact row matching, imputed missing categorical values with domain sentinels, parsed timestamps to ISO-8601 UTC, and normalized HTTP URL paths.
methods_tools: Pandas drop_duplicates, Domain-Specific Missing Value Imputation, urllib.parse Path Normalization, Datetime Vectorized Parsing.
result: 570,179 exact duplicate rows purged. Dataset reduced to 1,492,182 clean records. 18,433,649 missing values fully resolved. 0 invalid timestamps.

title: Basic Attack Classification
aim: To label access requests into 6 security classes (Benign vs Attacks) using deterministic regex signatures and temporal rolling windows.
process: Applied deterministic regex rules in strict priority (SQLi > Path Traversal > Command Injection > XSS > Brute Force > Benign). Detected brute-force via >=10 login attempts in a 10-minute sliding window per IP.
methods_tools: Regular Expression Matching, Temporal Rolling Windows (10-min sliding window), Deterministic Priority Hierarchy, Security Signature Auditing.
result: 1,487,823 Benign (99.71%) and 4,359 Attacks (0.29%). Attack breakdown: 1,342 Brute Force, 1,098 Path Traversal, 954 XSS, 805 Command Injection, 160 SQLi. 82 brute-force attacking IPs identified.

title: Feature Engineering & Anomaly Detection
aim: To engineer domain-specific, automated (Featuretools), and time-series (tsfresh) features, rank them via feature selection, and perform unsupervised anomaly detection.
process: Extracted request behavior, inter-request intervals, rolling rates, URL entropy, and payload features. Applied Featuretools DFS aggregations and tsfresh time-series stats. Trained Isolation Forest for unsupervised anomaly detection without target leakage.
methods_tools: Shannon Entropy Calculation, Vectorized Rolling Rates, Featuretools Deep Feature Synthesis, tsfresh Statistical Extraction, RandomForest Top 20 Feature Importance, Isolation Forest (contamination=auto).
result: 66 total features engineered. Isolation Forest scored all records: 98.0% Normal, 2.0% Anomalous. Anomaly detection independently identified abnormal request densities without label leakage.

title: Handling Imbalanced Dataset
aim: To resolve extreme class imbalance (9,298.89:1) between benign traffic and rare attack classes through sampling strategies.
process: Preserved 20% stratified test set untouched (298,437 records). Compared Random Undersampling, Random Oversampling, and SMOTE on the training split to synthesize minority attack vectors.
methods_tools: Stratified Train-Test Split (80/20), Random Undersampling, Random Oversampling, SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique), Class Distribution Auditing.
result: Evaluated 3 resampling paradigms. Produced a balanced training dataset of 60,000 records (10,000 per class across 6 classes) while preserving an untouched realistic test set of 298,437 records.

title: Data Wrangling & Aggregation
aim: To clean, reshape, filter, and aggregate multi-dimensional security telemetry for granular threat profiling.
process: Grouped traffic by client IP, analyzed hourly and daily attack frequencies, computed bot vs non-bot ratios, pivoted request types against attack labels, and identified high-risk IP subnets.
methods_tools: Pandas groupby, Pivot Tables, Temporal Resampling (Hourly / Daily), Multi-Level Indexing, Aggregation Profiling.
result: Aggregated 1,492,182 records into 59,497 wrangled IP security profiles. Pinpointed top persistent attacker IP 42.106.39.186 with high SQLi density. Quantified diurnal traffic patterns.

title: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
aim: To perform comprehensive statistical and behavioral exploratory data analysis across all traffic dimensions.
process: Generated 15 statistical plots covering univariate distributions, bivariate cross-tabulations, status code groupings, lexical URL and payload lengths, inter-arrival intervals, and feature correlations.
methods_tools: Seaborn & Matplotlib Visualization, Pearson Correlation Heatmap, Kernel Density Estimation (KDE), Logarithmic Frequency Scaling.
result: Identified strong correlation between high URL entropy and SQLi/Command Injection attacks. Discovered distinct inter-request delta clustering for automated scanners vs human traffic.

title: Attack Classification Models
aim: To train and compare multi-class machine learning classifiers (Random Forest vs Logistic Regression) for automated web attack detection.
input: 60,000 balanced training records and 298,437 untouched test records.
process: Trained Random Forest (100 estimators, max depth 20) and Logistic Regression on balanced features. Evaluated on the realistic, untouched 298,437 test dataset. Computed precision, recall, F1, and confusion matrices.
methods_tools: RandomForestClassifier, LogisticRegression, Scikit-Learn Classification Metrics, Stratified K-Fold Validation, Confusion Matrix Plotting.
result: Random Forest achieved 99.9705% overall test accuracy, 0.952579 Macro F1, and 0.999710 Weighted F1. Logistic Regression reached 97.0744% accuracy with 0.451820 Macro F1 due to non-linear feature interactions.

title: Reusable Log Processing Pipeline
aim: To integrate all log engineering phases into a production-grade, automated, modular, and auditable end-to-end data pipeline.
input: Raw honeypot JSON access log (cj.log), 215.40 MB, 2,061,431 records.
process: Executed 7 sequential stages: Streaming Load -> Positional Parsing -> Preprocessing/Deduplication -> Deterministic Labeling -> 26-Feature Engineering -> Automated Validation -> CSV & Parquet Serialization.
methods_tools: Object-Oriented Pipeline Architecture (LogProcessingPipeline), PyArrow Parquet Compression, 14 Integrity Validation Assertions, Structured Execution Profiling.
result: Successfully processed 2,061,431 raw records in 108.67 seconds. Parquet serialization reduced storage footprint by 97.8% (415 MB CSV to 9.1 MB Parquet). All 14 automated validation checks passed with 100% success.
output_evidence: pipeline_summary.json, pipeline_report.txt, feature_engineered_logs.parquet (9.1 MB), feature_engineered_logs.csv (415 MB).
